subject: Share variables between model and generated quantities?

messages.author: fb40a65bd21dcf6f
messages.subject: Share variables between model and generated quantities?
parts:
Hi,

I have some large covariance matrices I calculate from the parameters that I would like to access in the model and the generated quantities blocks. I can put them in the transformed parameters block but then I have memory problems as they are in all my samples. Is there any way to share them between the model and generated quantities? I guess I will just recalculate them but that seems like creating unnecessary work.

Thanks for any advice,
John.

messages.author: cab04b8f0759c712
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Share variables between model and generated quantities?
parts:
That's the right solution.

Don't worry about the extra computation done in the generated quantities block. It's done efficiently, without automatic differentiation, and it's done once per iteration. The model block not only executes it, calculated gradients using auto diff, but does this per leapfrog step, which is many times per iteration.

Besides, you can't do it any other way. I'm assuming you're in RStan? You should be able to do it from CmdStan.

Daniel

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Share variables between model and generated quantities?
parts:
In RStan, you can restrict the saved parameters to some subset,
so if if it's just memory, you could solve the problem that way.

If you do decide to compute something twice (as Daniel mentioned, the
computation in the generated quantities block is going to be something
like an order of magnitude faster), write the computation as a function
so it will remain in synch in the future if anything gets changed.

- Bob
